THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE  COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
Laxman S/O Chandrawwa vs Hussain S/O Imamsab Goundi And Anr on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121664557/
1  -2-  MFA No. 200684 of 2017  JUDGMENT
Though this appeal is listed for orders, with the consent of both counsel it is taken up for final disposal.

This appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation passed by MACT-XII,
Bijapur, (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC.No.1013/2010 dated 04.10.2011.
2.
For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.

3. The facts of the case are that on 06.02.2010 at about 17:00 p.m. when the petitioner was travelling in a maxi cab bearing Reg.No.KA-28/A-8899 and he was about to alight from the said cab,
at that time, cab was suddenly moved forward without any signal, the petitioner fell out from the vehicle and driver of the said cab ran over both legs of petitioner and caused accident.
Due to the said accident, petitioner has sustained fracture of right leg, injury to left leg, damage to urinary canal and sustained other injuries.
He claimed that he was treated as inpatient and that he spent money towards his medical treatment.
4. The claim petition was resisted by the insurer who generally denied the accident as well as the age and income of the injured.
It also denied the involvement of the offending vehicle.
5. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
6. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal after considering the notional monthly income of the claimant awarded compensation of Rs.30,000/-.

7. Being aggrieved by the quantum of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the present appeal is filed.
8.
The learned counsel for the claimant contended that having regard to the nature of the injuries sustained by the claimant, the Tribunal ought to have awarded adequate compensation.
9. Per contra, the learned counsel for the insurer supported the judgment and award of the Tribunal and therefore contended that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal be not disturbed.
10. It is seen that the owner/insurer had not challenged the judgment and award and therefore accepted the liability to pay the compensation.

11. Insofar as claim for compensation is concerned, injuries show that claimant had suffered Laxman S/O Chandrawwa vs Hussain S/O Imamsab Goundi And Anr on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121664557/

On perusal of the impugned judgment, the Tribunal has observed in para-9 as under:
"Issue No.2: In the light of observations made by me on issue No.1, the petitioner who has been examined as PW-1, he has reiterated the petition averments in his chief with respect to date, time and place of accident and injuries sustained by him and on account of said accident, he has sustained grievous injuries; to his right ankle joint,
fracture to right leg, injury to the left leg, damage to urinary canal and other injuries.

per the wound certificate Ex.P-5: compound fracture middle of right leg 4" x 1 cm and lacerated wound over the right heel 3" x skin deep and lacerated wound over right heel 3"x skin deep bleed, tenderness middle 3rd of left thigh, tenderness at hip and X-ray has been taken as per X-ray No.857 dtd: 7-2-10 and it shows pelvis, no fracture is seen and fracture of shaft lower 1/3rd of right tiller displacement, right foot no fracture is seen and
X-ray of right knee as per X-ray No.1039 dtd: 11-2-10 no fracture is seen and also X-ray of chest no fracture is seen.

Immediately after the accident, he has shifted to district Hospital, Bijapur for taking treatment as per wound certificate Ex.P-5 and among those injuries mentioned injury No.1 is grievous in nature and other injuries are simple in nature and to substantiate the case of the petitioner, he has also got examined the PW-2

Dr. S.S.Nagathan, who is Orthopaedician, as per the wound certificate, he has deposed that, he has treated the said injured in the Hospital and he has produced the case sheet of the injured which is marked as per Ex.P-7 wherein the said injured had been admitted as an indoor patient as pr IP NO.1199 from 6-2-10 to 8-3-10 and to substantiate the aforesaid injuries sustained by the petitioner and also x- ray has been taken during the course of taking treatment in the said hospital, the said case sheet contains x- ray films and among the 5 x-rays, the injury wherein, injury No.1 is fracture of middle of right leg whish is simple in gnat.

further, even though the PW-2 has deposed that, on account of said accidental injuries, sustained by him, he became permanently disabled and he himself is not able to do his day today work as he was doing prior.

As per the evidence of PW-1,
before the accident, he was working as a Patkari Le Class-4 employee in PWD and getting salary of Rs.15,000/-.
but, there is no any evid3nce that, he has not produced his pay slip etc., about the said his employment.

But, in his cross, he has categorically admitted that, till today he is serving as employee of the said PWD and there is no admissions with respect to his salary on account of said accidental injuries sustained by him when he himself has deposed that, there is no and loss of earnings with respect to his salary on account of said accidental injuries sustained by him,

even though, the PW-2 who has examined the said injured and assessing the disability by way of examining the said injured on 23-8-11 after lapse of 1 & 2 years from the date of accident and at the time of examination he has noticed that there is restrictions with respect to his movements relating to his right knee and ankle painful as per his examination notes noted in para No.3 of his examination in chief and at that time, he has also taken one x- ray as per Ex.P-8 wherein there is united fracture or lower 1/3 tibia and accordingly he has issued disability to the extent of 30 to 40$ related to right lower limb as per Ex.P-9. In his cross, he has deposed that, it is true at the time Laxman S/O Chandrawwa vs Hussain S/O Imamsab Goundi And Anr on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121664557/
3
of said accident the injured has admitted their Hospital, and he was aged about 57 years.

Further, it is true that, if the persons injured aged about more than 55 to 60 years, there will be variation with respect to injured completely curing on account of age factor defect that the persons who are aged below 50 years.
It is true that, they have discharged the said injured when he was fit for discharge.
Though he has deposed that, he has given two times follow up treatment.
But, he cannot say the said months follow up treatment and he has produced any documents to show that, he was under gone physiotherapy test.
Further, he deposed that, it is true, the aid percentage of disability if it compares to whole body, it will reduce.

Further, it is true that, the said surgical operation which has been conducted by him to the said injured was successfully and even till today there is implant is inserted and under such circumstances, he denied the suggestion that, he cannot assess the disability when implant is not removed from the body of the aid injured.
Further, with respect to loss of dependency is concerned.

Considering the loss of dependency, when the very PW-1 L himself has deposed that, till today he is not retired from his service, and there is no deduction from his salary on account of said accidental injuries sustained by him and therefore, there is no any loss of his income on account of said accidental injuries sustained by him.
While considering the said disability certificate as issued by the PW-2 does not arises.
Further, with respect to pain and suffering and also medical expenses and loss of his future earnings and loss of attendance and incidental expenses etc., is concerned.

Though, he has deposed that, on account of loss of mentally pain and suffering, he has incurred expenses to the extent of Rs.1,00,000/- and also loss future income of Rs.3,00,000/- medical expenses of Rs.50,000/-, but no any piece of documents with respect to medical expenses have been produced.

On the other hand, he has took treatment at district Hospital, wherein, free treatment will be provided and they may charge meager amount towards some accidental expenses and there is no any evidence that, how much he has actually incurred the medical expenses.
Further, he has deposed that, he has took follow up treatment at Dr. Kundaragi Hospital, but no any documents have been produced to that effect.

Even though there is no any evidence that, after discharge from the said Hospital as he has took one month treatment as per case sheet Ex.P-7, he has admitted on 6-2-10 and discharged on 8- 3-10 and during that period he might have been attended with one Attender and also he might have took further follow up treatment other than the government Hospital and during that period looking to the nature of injuries sustained by him, he might have incurred some medical expenses etc., looking to the name of injuries sustained by him, as per the case sheet and wound certificate in all he has sustained about 5 injuries among them first injury is grievous in nature and on account of said injuries sustained by him, as he was aged about 57 years at the time of accident, there he might have sustained some sort of pain and suffering therefore, awarding compensation towards pain and suffering to the extent of Rs.15,000/- is just and proper and during that period he might have attended with one Attender and considering the attendance charges per day Rs.100/- since he was took treatment at Laxman S/O Chandrawwa vs Hussain S/O Imamsab Goundi And Anr on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121664557/
4 district Hospital about 30 days as per case sheet Ex.P-7 and during that period, he might have also incurred some incidental expenses.
Hence, considering the attendance charges of Rs.3,000/- + Rs.2,000/- totally Rs.5,000/- is just and proper.

Further, with respect to future unhappiness, looking to the age of the injured, since he was aged about more than57 years at the time of accident, and even after his retirement he will get his pensionery benefits and therefore, considering the future unhappiness to the tune of Rs.5,000/- is just and proper.
Further, with respect to medical and other expenses is concerned.

Even though he has not produced any piece of documents about medical expenses but, looking to the nature of injuries sustained by him, he might have incurred some sort of medical expenses and therefore,
awarding the compensation to the tune of Rs.5,000/ towards medical and other incidental expenses is just and proper and therefore, in all awarding global compensation to the tune of Rs.30,000/- is just and proper."
12.

Considering the nature of injuries, period of treatment, medical bills, I am of the considered opinion that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be re- determined and re-calculated as under:-
Sl. Heads Amount awarded Amount awarded No by the Tribunal by this Court 1. Pain & sufferings Rs.30,000/-
2. Attendant, food, Rs.10,000/-
nourishment

etc charges 3. Loss of income during Rs.16,000/-
 laid up period Globally 4. Loss of amenities Rs.30,000/- Rs.30,000/-

To this extent, the appeal deserves to be modified and Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
(i) The Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The appellant is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.86,000/- as against Rs.30,000/-
Laxman S/O Chandrawwa vs Hussain S/O Imamsab Goundi And Anr on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121664557/
5 granted by the Tribunal together with interest - 10 - at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
(iii) Respondent/Insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount together with interest at 6% p.a. within a period of six weeks from the date of this order.
(iv) Vide order dated 23.03.2023, the appellant is not entitled for any interest on the enhanced compensation for the delayed period.
(v) Registry is directed to send a copy of this order to the Tribunal.

Sd/-
